description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled brings the authentic flavors of India right to your backyard. Succulent chicken pieces are marinated in a vibrant blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, then grilled to smoky perfection over hot charcoal. This iconic dish offers a delightful balance of tanginess, spice, and a charred exterior that makes it an irresistible centerpiece for any dinner.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken thoroughly and pat it completely dry with paper towels. Make deep gashes on the chicken pieces, especially on the thighs and breast, to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply. Set aside.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate for 1 hour.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another bowl, whisk together the yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, remaining lemon juice, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, remaining salt, black pepper, crushed fenugreek leaves, and optional red food color. Mix well until smooth. Add the chicken pieces to this second marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create a two-zone fire: one side with direct high heat and the other with indirect medium heat. Ensure the grill grates are clean and lightly oiled to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces on the direct heat side of the grill. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char. Then, move the chicken to the indirect heat side, close the lid, and cook for about 20-25 minutes, turning occasionally, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear.

instructions.title: Basting and Finishing
instructions.text: During the last 10 minutes of cooking, baste the chicken generously with mustard oil or melted butter. This adds flavor and helps create a beautiful, slightly crispy exterior. Continue grilling, turning and basting, until the chicken is cooked through and has a smoky, charred appearance.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro, and serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges and onion rings. It pairs wonderfully with naan, roti, or a simple green salad.

tips: For best flavor and tenderness, marinate the chicken for at least 6 hours, or preferably overnight, allowing the spices to deeply penetrate the meat.
Achieve the signature smoky flavor by adding wood chips to your charcoal grill. Soaking them in water for 30 minutes before use will help them smolder rather than burn quickly.
Serve Tandoori Chicken hot off the grill with fresh lemon wedges, onion rings, and a side of mint chutney or raita to complement its rich flavors.
article:
Unleash the captivating aromas and vibrant flavors of India right in your backyard with a show-stopping dish that tantalizes the senses: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This isn't just a meal; it's an experience, a culinary journey that brings the smoky essence of traditional Indian cooking to your dinner table. Forget bland chicken; we're talking about succulent, juicy pieces of chicken, marinated in a rich, spicy yogurt blend, then kissed by the flames of a charcoal grill until perfectly charred and unbelievably tender. As one of the most beloved Indian dinner recipes, Tandoori Chicken offers a perfect balance of heat, tang, and earthy spices, making it an ideal centerpiece for any gathering or a delightful weeknight treat. Get ready to transform your grilling game and impress everyone with this authentic, flavor-packed masterpiece.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is a world-renowned dish originating from the Indian subcontinent, traditionally cooked in a tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven. The intense heat of the tandoor, often fueled by charcoal or wood, gives the chicken its characteristic smoky flavor and beautifully charred exterior while keeping the inside incredibly moist. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we’re essentially replicating that authentic tandoor experience using a standard charcoal grill. The magic lies in the marinade: a vibrant concoction of yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and a complex array of spices like turmeric, red chili powder, cumin, coriander, and garam masala. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, while the spices infuse it with layers of unforgettable flavor. The high, direct heat of the charcoal grill provides the smoky char and crispy skin that makes this dish so iconic, creating a truly exceptional Indian dinner recipe that’s both rustic and refined.

## Ingredients You Need

To embark on your Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled adventure, gather these essential ingredients. The quality of your spices will significantly impact the final flavor, so opt for fresh, aromatic ones if possible.

For the Chicken:
*   2 lbs (approx. 1 kg) bone-in, skinless chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a mix are ideal)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice

For the Marinade (First Marination):
*   1 tablespoon ginger paste
*   1 tablespoon garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder

For the Marinade (Second Marination):
*   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt works well for thickness)
*   1 tablespoon ginger paste
*   1 tablespoon garlic paste
*   1 tablespoon Tandoori Masala powder (store-bought or homemade blend)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to desired spice level)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (adjust based on first marination and Tandoori Masala)
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1-2 tablespoons mustard oil (optional, for authentic flavor) or vegetable oil
*   A few drops of red food coloring (optional, for classic tandoori color)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create perfect Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken**: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make 2-3 deep slits on each piece of chicken with a sharp knife. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply.
2.  **First Marination**: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 2 tablespoons lemon juice, 1 tablespoon ginger paste, 1 tablespoon garlic paste, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, and 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder. Rub the marinade into the chicken, ensuring it gets into the slits. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
3.  **Second Marination**: While the chicken is marinating, prepare the second marinade. In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger paste, 1 tablespoon garlic paste, Tandoori Masala, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, black pepper, red chili powder, salt, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and mustard oil (if using). Add a few drops of red food coloring if you desire the classic vibrant red hue.
4.  **Combine Marinades**: Add the chicken from the first marination directly into the second marinade bowl. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare the Grill**: About 30-45 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for a two-zone cooking method – one side with direct high heat and the other with indirect medium heat. The grill temperature should be around 400-450°F (200-230°C). Clean the grill grates and oil them well to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken**: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the high heat side of the grill. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side, until you get a nice char.
7.  **Cook Through**: Once charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the lid and cook for 20-30 minutes, flipping occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C). The cooking time will vary depending on the size of your chicken pieces.
8.  **Final Char (Optional)**: For an extra smoky flavor and crispy finish, you can move the chicken back over direct heat for a final minute or two just before serving, being careful not to burn it.
9.  **Rest and Serve**: Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving truly spectacular Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled involves a few key techniques:

*   **Marination Time is Crucial**: The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavor it absorbs and the more tender it becomes. Aim for at least 6-8 hours, or even better, overnight.
*   **Dry Chicken is Key**: Before applying the first marinade, ensure your chicken is thoroughly patted dry. Excess moisture will dilute the marinade and prevent proper searing.
*   **Slit the Chicken**: Don't skip making deep slits in the chicken. This isn't just for show; it allows the marinade to penetrate deep into the meat, infusing every bite with flavor.
*   **Use Full-Fat Yogurt**: Full-fat yogurt provides a richer, creamier marinade that adheres better to the chicken and helps keep it moist during grilling. Greek yogurt is excellent for its thickness.
*   **Mind the Heat**: Start with high direct heat for that initial char, then move to indirect heat to cook the chicken through without burning the exterior. Patience is key for perfectly cooked Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled.
*   **Baste (Optional)**: Towards the end of cooking, you can brush the chicken lightly with a mixture of melted butter and a pinch of Tandoori Masala for added richness and shine.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill**: Cook in batches if necessary to ensure even cooking and proper charring. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it.

## Serving Suggestions

Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is fantastic on its own, but it truly shines when served as part of a complete Indian feast. Here are some classic accompaniments:

*   **Naan or Roti**: Essential for scooping up the flavorful chicken and any leftover juices. Warm, fluffy naan is a perfect pairing.
*   **Mint Chutney or Raita**: A cooling mint or coriander chutney, or a yogurt-based raita (cucumber, onion, or boondi raita), provides a refreshing contrast to the spicy chicken.
*   **Fresh Salad**: A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice and chaat masala) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Basmati Rice**: Plain steamed basmati rice or a light pilaf can help absorb the rich flavors.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Sliced Onions**: A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors, and thinly sliced red onions offer a pleasant bite.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a masterpiece, feel free to experiment with these variations:

*   **Different Meats**: The tandoori marinade works wonderfully with other proteins. Try it with bone-in lamb chops, fish fillets (marinate for less time, about 1-2 hours), or even paneer (Indian cheese) for a vegetarian option.
*   **Vegetarian Tandoori**: For a delicious meat-free alternative, use large chunks of paneer, mushrooms, bell peppers, and onions. Marinate for 1-2 hours and grill until tender and lightly charred.
*   **Spice Level**: Adjust the amount of red chili powder to suit your preference. For a milder version, reduce it; for more heat, add an extra dash. You can also add finely chopped green chilies to the second marinade for a fresh, fiery kick.
*   **Herbs**: Fresh fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) crushed and added to the second marinade lend a distinct, aromatic flavor commonly found in tandoori dishes.
*   **Grilling Alternatives**: No charcoal grill? No problem! You can achieve excellent results in a hot oven (preheat to 400°F/200°C, bake for 25-35 minutes, then broil for 5 minutes for char), under a broiler, or even in an air fryer. While these methods won't replicate the smoky flavor of charcoal, they will still yield delicious Tandoori chicken.

Mastering Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled at home is a rewarding culinary experience that brings the vibrant tastes of India to your dinner table. With its tender, flavorful chicken and irresistible smoky char, this Indian dinner recipe is guaranteed to become a family favorite. So fire up your grill, embrace the spices, and get ready to savor every mouthwatering bite!
